To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of Bloom’s Taxonomy in the writing of learning outcomes is a very useful tool for both lecturers and students.
the introduction of the learning outcomes into the teaching programme for science teachers is a positive step in the development of the programme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the relationship between learning outcome and competence?
the following issues: (1) the relationship between learning outcome statements and assessment of learning; and (2) the relationship between assessment of learning and assessment for learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the introduction of learning outcome-based assessment of students in teacher training has resulted in a more focused and effective programme for the student teacher and has resulted in more effective and more efficient teaching by the lecturer.
the introduction of learning outcome-based education has been successful in our teacher-training programme for the teaching of science.
the use of learning outcomes in the assessment of student science teachers' learning has had a significant effect on their learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a system for writing and assessing learning outcomes in science education that has been implemented in the science teacher training programme in the University of Limerick.
learning outcomes have been introduced into our science teaching programme and that they are now used to describe what students will be able to do as a result of their participation in a module.
the introduction of Learning Outcomes has led to a much more systematic approach to the writing of module descriptors, to teaching, and to assessment of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning outcomes of a course should be the same regardless of how it is assessed.

the learning outcomes are not only a useful tool in the process of curriculum development, but also a powerful instrument in the evaluation of the quality of teaching and learning in higher education.
the use of learning outcomes in the assessment of student achievement in teacher training programmes is not a straightforward matter.
